land.text: Northern Rhodesia: 'The territory of Zambia was known as "Northern Rhodesia" from 1911 to 1964'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws Northern Rhodesia inside its 'British East Africa' shape (1961-1968), which the british-east-africa dossier closes for Zambia at 24 October 1964.

capitals.name: Lusaka
capitals.note: Northern Rhodesia page: 'Capital: Livingstone (until 1935) Lusaka (from 1935)' and 'The capital was moved to Lusaka in 1935.' Zambia page: 'Capital and largest city: Lusaka'. Coordinates from the gazetteer (Natural Earth).

correction.text: Northern Rhodesia within its colonial frontiers, independent as the Republic of Zambia on 24 October 1964: the same land as the 1967 shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins 1967, three years after 'Northern Rhodesia became the Republic of Zambia on 24 October 1964'. The land lies inside Cliopatria's British East Africa shape until 1968; that overlap is for the british-east-africa dossier to resolve.

747,138 km2 for 1967-2023 against the infobox 'Total: 752,617 km2' (ratio 0.99; the Northern Rhodesia page gives 751,925 km2). Gazetteer: 2,470 cells against 2,501 for modern Zambia. The pages describe no change of frontier after the colonial boundary treaties. The row's listed modern countries (DRC, Angola) are overlap of cells along the frontier, not territory.

ledger.note: 24 October 1964: Northern Rhodesia becomes the independent Republic of Zambia under Kenneth Kaunda. 'Northern Rhodesia became the Republic of Zambia on 24 October 1964, with Kenneth Kaunda as the first president.' The Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland, which it had joined in 1953, 'was formally dissolved on 31 December 1963' (Northern Rhodesia page).

wars.name: Rhodesian Bush War (Zambian front)
wars.outcome: No territory changed hands. Zambia hosted Nkomo's ZIPRA; Rhodesian forces raided across the frontier; the war ended with the Lancaster House Agreement and a cease-fire announced 21 December 1979.
wars.note: Bush War page: 'Rhodesian external operations extended into Zambia after Nkomo's ZIPRA nationalists shot down two unarmed' aircraft; 'attacked the ZIPRA guerrilla base at Westlands farm near Lusaka in October 1978'. Zambia page: Kaunda's support for the guerrillas 'led to political tension and the militarisation of the border, culminating in its closure in 1973', and 'Rhodesia responded with Operation Gatling, an attack on Nkomo's guerrilla bases in Zambia' (undated on the page). The raids were not occupations, so no contest or occupation zone is drawn.

certainty.note: The frontier is the colonial one fixed by treaty: with the Congo 'fixed by a treaty in 1894', with Angola 'not fixed until 1905', and the short frontier with German South-West Africa by the 1890 Anglo-German Convention (Northern Rhodesia page). No page opened records a change after 1964.

sources.title: Zambia
sources.note: Identity, 24 October 1964 independence, area 752,617 km2, Lumpa uprising, Rhodesian border closure 1973, Operation Gatling.

sources.title: Northern Rhodesia
sources.note: The colony before 1964: BSAC rule, 1924 protectorate, Lusaka from 1935, the Federation 1953-1963, boundary treaties of 1890, 1894 and 1905.

sources.title: Rhodesian Bush War
sources.note: The war's span and the Zambian raids (Westlands farm near Lusaka, October 1978); cited for the war entry only.

notes: Cliopatria row 'Zambia' begins 1967 against independence on 24 October 1964, so a 1964-1966 keyframe is added; it overlaps British East Africa (1961-1968) in 1967-1968. The Lumpa uprising ('an uprising in the north of the country known as the Lumpa Uprising led by Alice Lenshina', after the January 1964 election) is not dated more closely by the page and held no land the page names, so no rebel dossier or ledger event. The Northern Rhodesia page did not carry the Barotseland Agreement of 1964 or January 1964 self-government. The pages record no border change with the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Zaire, Malawi, Mozambique, Zimbabwe, Botswana, Namibia or Angola. Rulers omitted (the page gives Kaunda as first president; no complete list was read). Page budget: two pages plus the Rhodesian Bush War page shared with the rhodesia dossier. native_names left empty: no page read gives one.
